We got a list of templates. Need the one that when applied to our target molecule yields the precursors we have. The target molecule likely matches product_smiles in these entries: many have product_smiles pattern '[O:1]=[C:2]([OH:3])[CH:4]=[CH:5][c:6]1...'. That is a cinnamic acid derivative (alpha,beta-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic). Our product likely is that. So the template ID we need is the template used earlier. Which one of these corresponds to Doebner modification? Probably the first entry reaction_id 19640. It has mapped_rxn and template_hash. We need template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The result dict includes 'reaction_id' but not template_id. Maybe template_id is same as reaction_id? In other tasks, template_id is integer. Likely use reaction_id as template_id. So we can pick 19640.

Thus answer: mapped_rxn from that entry and template_id 19640.

Let's extract mapped_rxn: '[OH-].[Na+].Cl.[O:1]=[C:2]1[O:3]C(C2=[CH:5][CH:4]=C(O)C=C2)(C2=CC=C(O)C=C2)[C:11]2=[C:6]1[CH:7]=[CH:8][CH:9]=[CH:10]2.CCO>>[O:1]=[C:2]([OH:3])[CH:4]=[CH:5][c:6]1[cH:7][cH:8][cH:9][cH:10][cH:11]1'
